The flag of Israel, also known as the "Star of David" or "Shield of David," consists of a white background with a large blue hexagram (six-pointed star) in the center. The hexagram is composed of two overlapping equilateral triangles, forming a star shape. The blue color is known as "King's Blue" and is reminiscent of the color used in the ancient Hebrew garments of royalty.

The flag was officially adopted on December 5, 1948, shortly after the establishment of the State of Israel. The design is based on a symbol that has been used by Jews for centuries, appearing on Jewish ceremonial objects and documents. The Star of David is believed to represent the unity and strength of the Jewish people.

The proportions of the flag are 2:3, meaning the width is two-thirds the length of the flag. The white and blue colors are significant in Jewish tradition, with white symbolizing purity and blue representing the sky and the divine.
